profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC4 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.

reading.body:
Equinix DC4 is a 60,590-square-foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's multi-building Ashburn campus in Data Center Alley, Loudoun County. The operator publishes no power capacity figure for this specific building. Equinix's DC2 building on the same campus, cited as representative of campus general specifications, supports a minimum cabinet density of 4 kilovolt-amperes, which at typical AI training loads of 40 kilowatts per rack would imply roughly 10 racks per cabinet; the actual IT load and accelerator count at DC4 remain unknown without published power data.

Data Center Alley in Loudoun County is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix's Ashburn campus anchors one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities represent a major regional cluster, though only 23 publish power capacity figures; those 23 facilities account for 1,375 megawatts of published capacity statewide, and this campus ranks 24th by published megawatts, below the threshold of public disclosure in Virginia's current data.

The facility holds certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High, though these are confirmed only for DC2 as representative of campus general specifications and not explicitly published for DC4 itself. Without published power figures or building-specific certifications, DC4's significance to AI scaling cannot be directly assessed from Equinix's public specification page, though its location in Data Center Alley and its position within a campus serving a top-three peering market on the East Coast places it in one of the continent's most strategically connected data center regions.
